title: Exact Mayer-Vietoris sequences with pullback-compatible connecting maps
statement: Let g:Y→X be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], U,V opens of X with U∪V=X, and G an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Use cohomology pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] with the coefficient composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] for all restriction maps and for P_I on I=U∩V. There exist connecting homomorphisms delta_X^q:H^q(I,G restricted to I)→H^{q+1}(X,G) and delta_Y^q:H^q(g^{-1}I,(g^{-1}G) restricted to g^{-1}I)→H^{q+1}(Y,g^{-1}G) for all q≥0. On X and Y the restriction-to-two-opens map is injective in degree zero; restriction to the pair, difference of intersection restrictions, delta, and next-degree restriction are exact at each adjacent pair. Moreover delta_Y^q(P_I(x))=g^*(delta_X^q(x)). No ordinary restriction square is part of this statement. The intersection on Y is g^{-1}(U∩V), identified with g^{-1}U∩g^{-1}V.

source.place: Tag 0A50, proof, short exact complexes of sections. Pullback compatibility is agent-written. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A50 because the literature checkout is absent locally.

proof.text: Obtain compatible short exact nonnegative section complexes and additive homology identifications intertwining the four horizontal maps and the two vertical maps. This uses no connecting map.

Define delta_X and delta_Y by conjugating the Mathlib homology connecting maps with the intersection and global additive equivalences. The three homology_exact lemmas give exactness, and exact_transport transfers their kernel/image characterizations to the prescribed horizontal maps. The initial homology restriction is mono because there is no differential entering degree zero and the complex map is mono; the additive equivalences transport its injectivity.

Apply delta_naturality to the morphism of short exact complexes. Express an intersection class as eCX(z), use the two vertical comparison identities, and cancel eCY followed by its inverse in the definition of delta_Y. The resulting equality is precisely delta_Y(P_I(x))=g*(delta_X(x)).
